UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user's profile in the Nadajuda application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity (matches Firebase Auth UID).

personalNotes.description: Personal notes or information provided by the user.

CompetitionTime.title: CompetitionTime
CompetitionTime.description: Represents the time recorded for a specific athlete in a competition.

id.description: Unique identifier for the CompetitionTime entity.

time.description: The recorded time for the competition event (in seconds).

Workout.title: Workout
Workout.description: Represents a workout session containing multiple items.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Workout entity.

name.description: Name of the workout session (e.g., 'Treino de Velocidade').

workoutItems.description: An array of workout items that make up the session.

WorkoutItem.title: WorkoutItem
WorkoutItem.description: Represents a single row in a workout table.

repeticoes.description: Number of repetitions for the set.

observacoes.description: Optional observations, like equipment used or rest time.

temposRegistrados.description: An array of recorded times for repetitions, where the value is the time.

Event.title: Event
Event.description: Represents a specific swimming event or competition.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Event entity.

stroke.description: Swimming stroke used in the event (e.g., Freestyle, Backstroke).

params.name: userId

definition.description: Stores workouts created by each user. Includes denormalized 'userProfileId' for authorization independence. A workout contains an array of WorkoutItems.

params.name: userProfileId

firestore.reasoning: The Firestore structure is designed to manage user profiles, competition times, and detailed workouts. User profiles are stored under `/users/{userId}`. Competition times and workouts are stored as subcollections under the user's profile to ensure data ownership. The Workout entity now contains an array of embedded WorkoutItem objects, reflecting the new table-based structure for workout details. This avoids creating a separate subcollection for workout items, simplifying data retrieval for a whole workout session. Events remain global. This design enforces clear ownership, simplifies security rules, and supports the requested editable table structure for workouts.
